problem: The direction of the gate voltage is wrong. For a p-type body, accumulation happens when VG is BELOW the flat-band voltage; there the negative gate charge attracts holes to the surface. A positive gate (VG above VFB) repels holes and gives depletion, not accumulation. As written, the text says 'Raise VG above VFB... the positive gate charge attracts holes, and they pile up at the surface', which contradicts both the physics and the lead of the chapter.
fix: For a p-type body, accumulation needs VG below VFB. The negative gate charge attracts holes and they pile up at the surface, so the capacitor stores charge like a normal plate capacitor. Raise VG above VFB and the positive gate repels the holes. The surface is left with no free carriers, and a depletion region of ionised acceptors grows to a width Wd.

problem: The question asks for the three states 'as the gate voltage rises above the flat-band voltage'. Rising above VFB gives depletion and then inversion only; accumulation lies below VFB. The answer repeats the same mistake ('Accumulation: VG just above VFB, holes pile at the surface'), so the quiz is wrong as set.
fix: Q1: Name the three states of the MOS capacitor with a p-type body as VG moves from below VFB upward, and give the condition for each. Answer: Accumulation: VG < VFB, holes pile at the surface. Depletion: VG > VFB, holes are pushed away and a depletion region of width Wd opens. Inversion: the surface potential reaches 2φF and an electron channel forms.

problem: The comparison signs have been lost in three cells, so the table reads 'VGS T' and 'VDS GS − VT', which is meaningless. The nMOS cutoff row reads 'VGS T' instead of 'VGS < VT', the nMOS linear row reads 'VDS GS − VT' instead of 'VDS < VGS − VT', and the pMOS cutoff and linear rows lost their '<' as well.
fix: Cutoff: nMOS VGS < VT; pMOS VGS > VT. Linear: nMOS VGS > VT and VDS < VGS − VT; pMOS VGS < VT and VDS > VGS − VT. Saturation: nMOS VGS > VT and VDS ≥ VGS − VT; pMOS VGS < VT and VDS ≤ VGS − VT.

problem: The '<' signs are missing, so the answer reads 'Cutoff: VGS T. Linear: VGS > VT and VDS GS − VT', which a student cannot use.
fix: Cutoff: VGS < VT. Linear: VGS > VT and VDS < VGS − VT. Saturation: VGS > VT and VDS ≥ VGS − VT.

problem: Part of the answer text has been lost: it reads 'VDS = 0.5 V D = 500 µA/V² × ...', with the region test and the start of the current formula missing, so the reasoning cannot be followed. The final number 187.5 µA is correct.
fix: Overdrive = 1.6 − 0.6 = 1.0 V, positive, so the device is not in cutoff. VDS = 0.5 V is less than VGS − VT = 1.0 V, so the device is in the linear region. ID = kn′(W/L)[(VGS − VT)VDS − VDS²/2] = 500 µA/V² × [(1.0 V)(0.5 V) − (0.5 V)²/2] = 500 × (0.5 − 0.125) µA = 187.5 µA.

problem: The powers of ten are typed as plain text: 'k = 1.38×10−23 J/K', 'q = 1.6×10−19 C', 'ni ≈ 1010 cm−3', 'NA (unit: cm−3)'. On a phone these read as '10 minus 23' and '1010' rather than 1.38×10⁻²³ J/K and 10¹⁰ cm⁻³.
fix: Write the exponents with the sup tag: k = 1.38×10<sup>−23</sup> J/K, q = 1.6×10<sup>−19</sup> C, n<sub>i</sub> ≈ 10<sup>10</sup> cm<sup>−3</sup>, N<sub>A</sub> in cm<sup>−3</sup>.

problem: The symbol VT is used here for the thermal voltage kT/q, but VT is defined everywhere else in the chapter as the threshold voltage. The same answer also writes 'nie^(φF/VT)', so a student meets two different VT meanings within one sentence.
fix: Use a separate symbol, for example: the electron concentration at the surface becomes n<sub>i</sub>e^(φ<sub>F</sub>/V<sub>th</sub>) = N<sub>A</sub>, where V<sub>th</sub> = kT/q is the thermal voltage.
